target.definition: Total visitor arrivals to Hong Kong during September 2026, as first reported provisionally by the Hong Kong Tourism Board.

inputs.name: annual_arrivals_2025
inputs.description: Total visitor arrivals to Hong Kong in calendar year 2025

provenance.rationale: HKTB 2024 arrivals were ~44.5M; 2025 trending modestly higher toward ~46M

inputs.name: september_share_of_year
inputs.description: Fraction of annual arrivals falling in September

provenance.rationale: September is a shoulder month; roughly 1/12 of the year with slight dip

inputs.name: yoy_growth_factor
inputs.description: Year-over-year growth factor from 2025 to 2026 arrivals

provenance.rationale: Continued recovery/growth in inbound tourism, single-digit percent

inputs.name: daily_arrivals
inputs.description: Average daily visitor arrivals to Hong Kong in September 2026

inputs.name: days_in_september
inputs.description: Number of days in September

inputs.name: mainland_share
inputs.description: Share of arrivals from mainland China

provenance.rationale: Mainland typically ~75% of HK inbound visitors

inputs.name: mainland_arrivals_sep
inputs.description: Mainland Chinese visitor arrivals in September 2026

inputs.name: non_mainland_arrivals_sep
inputs.description: Non-mainland visitor arrivals in September 2026

provenance.rationale: Short-haul and long-haul markets combined, ~25% share

inputs.name: hk_population
inputs.description: Population of Hong Kong

provenance.source: Hong Kong Census and Statistics Department
provenance.quote: Population of Hong Kong was about 7.5 million

inputs.name: visitors_per_resident_per_year
inputs.description: Annual visitor arrivals per Hong Kong resident

inputs.name: september_fraction_of_year
inputs.description: Fraction of the year represented by September

paths.description: Allocate 2026 annual arrivals down to September using seasonal share
Daily arrivals times days in September
Scale from resident population via arrivals-per-resident, then to September; cross-check with mainland/non-mainland split

problems: path p3: dimension mismatch: the formula gives count per time (s**-1), but the target needs a pure number, a count or a share (dimensionless). The formula has one 'per time' more than the target; inputs with a time unit in this path: visitors_per_resident_per_year ('arrivals/person/year'). If the target is a total over a period, multiply by an input whose unit is a length of time: the period itself (for example days_in_period with unit 'day'), or period_length = 1 with unit 'year' when a share of the year then picks the part you need. A share, or a ratio such as 'days/year', has no time unit and does not cancel it.
